body.statement: Can the handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{multi}}\) be developed into an adaptive recovery map that identifies every normalized source direction when each moment-determinate non-Gaussian source has some informative cumulant order but no common order is nonzero and separating for all sources, while retaining simultaneous valid inference for \(\mathcal R_{xy}(C)\)?
body.justification: This question exposes the genuine unresolved step between full-law OICA information and a practicable finite-moment causal-frontier procedure.
body.gap: VirtaNordhausenOja2016 combines third and fourth cumulants only for square ICA, and PodosinnikovaEtAl2019 aggregates generating-function Hessians without a source-specific-order causal-set limit theory.
body.consumer: A solution would remove the common-cumulant-order restriction for overcomplete latent LiNG effect analysis.
